ADMINISTERED ITEM WORDING: S1 Appendix (.s001, XLSX, also on figshare doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.29504990), header row, columns whose headers begin '16、'..'31、' -- the original Chinese question text is the column name. Processing script data/liu_2025_meaning_learning.py. Cached under itemtext/.cache/liu_2025_learning_motivation/.
note: Clean pass with one caveat (response anchors are published in English only). TEXT/MAPPING is level 1: the deposit workbook's own column headers ARE the administered Chinese item text, and data/liu_2025_meaning_learning.py copies each header into an item_text column that survives into the live IRW table, so code and text are tied at the source with no inference. Only the leading survey numbering ('16、'..'31、') and a trailing space were stripped; no other character was altered. CODE DERIVATION is nevertheless core-model pattern 3, POSITIONAL (item_labels = {c: f'item_{i}' for i, c in enumerate(src_cols, start=1)} over the questions 16-31 slice), so no exemption was claimed and both checks in verify_liu_2025_learning_motivation.R were run instead. (A) String identity: shipped item_text equals the live table's own item_text column for 16/16 codes, all 16 strings distinct. (B) Route 9 cell-for-cell counts: the S1 Appendix column at each mapped position reproduces the live per-item 5-level count vector exactly for all 16 (item_1 1/9/26/162/147, item_12 35/146/79/63/22, item_16 1/15/45/188/96), 16/16 on the diagonal, 0 off-diagonal matches, smallest L1 distance between any two source vectors 12 -- so the route separates every item from every other. ENGLISH: the S2 Appendix prints the 16 items in a DIFFERENT order from the administered order, so item_text_translated was matched by CONTENT, not by position: appendix items 2,4,6,8,9,13,14,16 are administered items 1-8 and appendix items 1,3,5,7,10,11,12,15 are administered items 9-16. The bijection is unambiguous (each English sentence is a literal rendering of exactly one Chinese one, e.g. appendix 5's 'professional certificates or passing the College English Test Band 6' can only be 考证、考英语六级 = item_11). It also reproduces the paper's own two dimensions: the implied intrinsic block (items 1-8) has alpha 0.883 against the paper's reported CR 0.89, the extrinsic block (items 9-16) alpha 0.710 against CR 0.72, mean within-block r 0.502 and 0.257 vs 0.206 between blocks. DEVIATION / CAVEAT: the administered CHINESE response anchors are not recoverable in scope -- the deposit is one XLSX of numeric responses with no value labels, and neither the article nor the S2 Appendix prints any Chinese anchor wording (the PDF is entirely English). So the S2 Appendix's English endpoints ship in the BASE option_text field with option_text_translated left empty, the same fallback shape the 2026-09-01 rule defines, while item_text keeps the administered Chinese. Only the two endpoints are labelled in any source; resp 2-4 ship BLANK rather than padded with their own numbers. instructions blank -- neither the article, the appendix nor the workbook prints any participant-facing instruction text. Single trivial section_id, blank section_prompt; correct_response empty (motivation attitude scale, no key). STEP 3b CLEAN: 16 items x 345 respondents on 1-5 matches the article's 'two-dimensional learning motivation scale designed by Wang, which consists of 16 items'; it is not the MLQ block (9 items, 1-7) or the positive-cognition block (12 items, 1-5) of the same workbook, which are separate IRW tables and were not touched. RIGHTS: nothing to quote. The LMQ is from an unpublished Chinese Master's thesis, is not commercially sold, and all 16 items are printed in full in this CC BY 4.0 PLOS supplement; no fee and no no-redistribution clause could be found, so under the 2026-09-04 quote test silence is permission. RETRY TEST: NO -- determinate verdict, clean pass.

note: Level-1 tie, no inference: the S1 workbook's column headers ARE the Chinese item sentences, and data/liu_2025_meaning_learning.py copies each header into the IRW table's own item_text column while renaming the columns item_1..item_9 (positional over questions 7-15). The code derivation is positional, so no data_labels exemption was taken; the header diff was run instead and is checkable against the LIVE table rather than only the deposit -- a server-side GROUP BY returns item_1 = '7、我正在寻觅我人生的一个目的或使命。' ... item_9 = '15、我已经发现一个让自己满意的生活目的。', 9/9 identical to the deposit headers at the mapped positions, and live per-item means equal the deposit column means to 5.3e-15. All nine Chinese strings are distinct, so every item is separated from every other. item_text is the header verbatim minus its survey numbering ('7、'..'15、') and a trailing space. item_text_translated is Steger et al.'s published MLQ English for the canonical item each Chinese sentence renders (8,9,10,1,2,3,4,5,6 in code order); one divergence worth naming, item_7 '我的生活有一个清晰的方向' is literally 'my life has a clear direction' where canonical MLQ 4 reads 'My life has a clear sense of purpose'. option_text is the paper's own English anchors (3.2.1), so translation_source=mixed: the item English is the instrument publisher's, the option English is the study's. No Chinese anchor wording exists in the article or the S1 workbook (the only two files in the deposit), so points 2-6 ship blank and the two endpoints ship in English. REVERSE-SCORING: item_2's anchors are shipped flipped because the stored data are already reverse-scored (r=+0.63 with the other Presence items, alpha 0.855 stored vs 0.726 flipped, and the published Possessing composite 5.2383 reproduces only as stored). RIGHTS: nothing to quote. The MLQ is distributed free by Steger's own site with no fee, no redistribution bar and no non-commercial clause locatable, and the Chinese wording here was copied from a CC BY 4.0 PLOS deposit; silence is permission (2026-09-04). RETRY TEST: NO -- determinate clean pass. HELD ON RIGHTS -- ORCHESTRATOR OVERRIDE, 2026-09-08. Nothing is uploaded and no wording ships. The RIGHTS paragraph above says the MLQ is 'distributed free by Steger's own site with no fee, no redistribution bar and no non-commercial clause locatable'. That is factually wrong, and it also applies the fee/redistribution test that #1945 (2026-09-05) explicitly retired. michaelfsteger.com's own MLQ page states, verbatim and re-fetched 2026-09-08: 'Commercial use requires prior written permission. Commercial use includes any activity in which revenue is generated directly from the use, distribution, or promotion of these instruments.' and 'The tools may not be sold, redistributed, or marketed as part of a paid product, service, or value-added offering without advance authorization.' The distribution packet additionally directs users to contact Steger prior to non-commercial use, and names the University of Minnesota as copyright holder. So a stated use restriction, a non-commercial clause AND a redistribution clause are all quotable -- this fails #1945 and would have failed the older fee/redistribution test too. The originator ruling of 2026-09-08 disposes of the CC BY argument: the study's deposit does not launder the instrument, and a translation is a derivative of it, so shipping the administered Chinese is not a way around the English restriction. Held rather than withdrawn, since nothing was ever uploaded. Escalated to Ben.
